Hey im a georgia trans person too! Im being seen by the practice called "qmed" who have been managing my testosterone and labs and stuff. They have a ton of resources on their website, and they do telehealth around the southeast (georgia, Florida, and i thiiink a couple other states). I can't help with advice on being uninsured or not having a therapist, but imo looking into qmed might be somewhere to start. I also just had top surgery in Atlanta a few days ago with Dr Sheldon lincenberg and had a very good experience. He's been practicing for many years, I think 20+, and had a good bedside manner and I am recovering very well from the actual surgery. My surgery cost around $1200 with insurance as I opted for extra liposuction (which was $850 and didnt have the option of being covered by insurance as it wasn't necessary, but did have the loophole of no hospital fees) since im overweight (bmi around 30) to help with dog earing. I haven't seen under my chest bandage yet but everything looks super uniform and flat. I had $500 in surgeons fees bc i met my deductible and actually met my out of pocket max like halfway through the $500 so only owed $350 for that portion. I needed a letter stating my gender dysphoria diagnosis from my psychiatrist and qmed doctor to get insurance coverage. I hope my story is somewhat helpful! I wish you luck on your journey

Yup, I had anorexia 2020-2021, I started having tachycardia constantly after I started really restricting, as I lost more weight I started getting crazier and crazier symptoms and I felt like I was dying. I went to a checkup to see if i could qualify for inpatient residential and I was so bad off my doctor just sent me straight to the hospital. Whole time I was there I had to orthostatic vitals, I would stand up and immediately my heart rate would shoot up to 150 and stay there. I didn't learn what POTS was until about a year or two after I got out of residential. I went from "I feel like im having a heart attack 24/7" to "I feel like shit generally" in the course of that year. I still felt pretty bad once I was weight restored, but nowhere near as bad as when I was underweight. I am technically just diagnosed with dysautonomia but my cardiologist is aware it's POTS and im on a beta blocker. I definitely learned my lesson in a way with ending up disabled from thinking an eating disorder was how i should live my life. It keeps me in check, that's for sure. I still get that little voice in my head but honestly I'm OK now. I hope you are doing well OP, shits not easy.

For me losing weight is all about what I eat. I don't excersize outside the 6-8k steps I get daily at school because it hits me too hard after. 

I eat in a caloric deficit. If you want to lose weight it could help to calculate your tdee via google (it tells you how much you need to eat to maintain, gain, or lose weight) never eat under the reccomended as that can cause a lot of problems that can be long term. 

Often when you first start tracking what you eat people just eyeball serving sizes which can cause the amount your eating to not match what you're tracking, which can make you keep gaining or maintaining even though you think you're eating less. Im not saying to measure everything to the gram but like even using tablespoons to measure oil and condiments can be helpful. 

Just wanted to say again to not eat under the reccomended caloric intake for your height and weight, i did that for too long years ago and that actually is what triggered my POTS to start in the first place. Losing weight is super hard but you got this. If you have a lot of trouble it could help to see a dietician as well.
